zh: 无论怎么选择删除，任一时刻剩余括号的总数都相同；不同选择只影响差值 D=左括号数−右括号数。而所有可达的 D 奇偶性相同，并且构成步长为 2 的连续区间。
所以不必保存所有状态，只维护剩余总数 T 和可达差值区间的两端 low、high。读到括号时整体平移；读到数字 d 时，令 r=min(d,T)，分别从最小和最大差值的状态推出新区间的两端。
T=low=high=0；遇到 ( 则 T、low、high 各加一，遇到 ) 则 T 加一、low 和 high 各减一；遇到数字 d：r=min(d,T)，若 r>0 则 low=max(r−T, low−r)，high=min(T−r, high+r)，再 T−=r；扫描完若 T 为偶数且 low≤0≤high 输出 1，否则输出 0。
en: Whatever deletions are chosen, the total number of remaining parentheses at any moment is the same; the choices only affect the difference D = (number of '(') - (number of ')'). All reachable values of D have the same parity and form a contiguous interval with step 2.

So there is no need to keep every state: maintain only the remaining total T and the endpoints low and high of the reachable difference interval. A parenthesis shifts the whole interval; for a digit d let r = min(d, T) and derive the new endpoints from the states with the smallest and the largest difference.

Set T = low = high = 0; on ( add one to T, low and high; on ) add one to T and subtract one from low and high; on a digit d: r = min(d, T), and if r > 0 set low = max(r - T, low - r), high = min(T - r, high + r), then T -= r; after the scan print 1 if T is even and low <= 0 <= high, otherwise 0.

explanationEn:
## Approach

Scan from left to right, maintaining the current number T of surviving parentheses and, over all reachable choices, the minimum low and maximum high of the difference D = (left parentheses) - (right parentheses). All reachable differences have the same parity and form a contiguous interval with step 2, so there is no need to store every state. On a parenthesis, T and both interval endpoints change by 1. On a digit d, let r = min(d, T). The smallest difference the minimum-difference state can leave is low - r (when it has at least r left parentheses), otherwise r - T; the largest difference the maximum-difference state can leave is high + r (when it has at least r right parentheses), otherwise T - r. Then T decreases by r. At the end, 0 lies in [low, high] exactly when some deletion choice leaves equal numbers of the two kinds of parentheses.

## Proof of correctness

Prove by induction that the set of reachable differences is always a contiguous interval of one parity. The initial state has only difference 0. Appending `(` or `)` shifts every difference by 1, which keeps the property. When processing a digit, fix an old difference D with O open and C close parentheses; deleting r parentheses can choose the number x of deleted open parentheses with max(0, r - C) <= x <= min(r, O), and the new difference is D + r - 2x, so it forms a contiguous interval with step 2. The endpoints for this state simplify to L(D) = max(r - T, D - r) and U(D) = min(T - r, D + r), where T = O + C. Each time the old reachable D increases by 2, L and U each increase by at most 2; moreover U(D) >= L(D + 2) - 2, so the results of neighbouring states touch or overlap on the step-2 lattice of differences. The global minimum is attained from D = low and the global maximum from D = high, so the new endpoints are max(r - T, low - r) and min(T - r, high + r), exactly the update formulas used in the implementation. Therefore the endpoints fully represent all reachable states. After the scan, there is a state with equal numbers of left and right parentheses if and only if the difference interval contains 0 and the remaining total is even.

## Complexity

Time O(n), extra space O(1).

## Correction of a source error

The original LeetCode Google interview post and the fixed OAMaster snapshot both list `())` as a balanced example, but it has 2 left parentheses and 1 right parenthesis, which directly contradicts the same statement's definition that the numbers of left and right parentheses are equal; the example is marked as a source error and not followed. Under the explicit definition, `())` outputs 0 and `)(` outputs 1. The original post explains that a digit deletes any d parentheses to its left and that consecutive digits are processed one by one; its example `)(1` may delete either parenthesis to its left. The snapshot's implementations in three languages delete all existing parentheses when d exceeds the number currently available, and this site keeps that observable behaviour.

[OAMaster problem snapshot](https://oamaster.com/docs/companies/google#37-is-balanced-string); [original LeetCode Google interview post](https://leetcode.com/discuss/post/6582615/google-phone-screen-by-ashokkumarmula422-qjfm/).

Added by this site: standard input is one line, length 1..200000, containing only `(`, `)` and `0`..`9`; if a digit exceeds the number of parentheses not yet deleted before it, all surviving parentheses are deleted. The original problem gives no length range or input/output protocol.
